messages.author: 9ff02ee016b8a9e0
messages.subject: insets of non-ggplot2 plots
parts:
Dear ggploters,

I am trying to plot two insets on a ggplot, where the insets are
phylogenetic trees of species. The below example uses the ggplot2
economics dataset, and I generate two random trees. Is there a way to
add foreign plot types as insets on ggplots?

################
require(ape)
require(ggplot2)
data(economics)

(b <- qplot(uempmed, unemploy, data = economics) +
geom_smooth(se = F))

tree1 <- rtree(20) # generate random tree of 20 species
tree2 <- rtree(20) # generate another random tree of 20 species
plot(tree1) # visualize tree 1
plot(tree2) # visualize tree 2

# Trying to plot these trees does not work. "print" in package ape
just prints the tree to the console
subvp1 <- viewport(width = 0.4, height = 0.4, x = 0.75, y = 0.35)
subvp2 <- viewport(width = 0.4, height = 0.4, x = 0.35, y = 0.75)
b
print(tree1, vp = subvp1)
print(tree2, vp = subvp2)



Thanks! Scott

messages.author: 881c51ed14655bd5
messages.subject: Re: insets of non-ggplot2 plots
parts:
Scott,

What you are asking to do is very complicated.   First you are trying to mix base graphics (plot) with grid graphics (qplot/ggplot).  Afaik, this cannot be done.  check Paul Murrell's book R graphics.  What you need if you want to do this is either find or write a procedure for visualizing the trees as a grid grob object.  Grobs can then be included through viewports into other grid plots like ggplot.

-Andrew

messages.author: 0fe05797d4947712
messages.subject: Re: insets of non-ggplot2 plots
parts:
It sounds like a cool project, but I agree that it sounds difficult.
Is there a reason why the plot needs to be inset before outputting
from R?

I often do things like this by combining two plots in Adobe
Illustrator or some similar vector graphics program. I will admit that
I've not tried this with R plots and don't know much about exporting
as a vector graphics format (.ps, .eps, .svg, etc...) but it looks
like it isn't hard to output plots in these formats. I often spruce up
Excel graphs by exporting as a PDF and opening them in Illustrator,
where it opens as a multilayer vector image. It's amazing how not-
Excel you can make an Excel chart look this way. And when you are done
you can save it at whatever size you like without losing quality.

You could do the same things in an image editor like photoshop using
pixel based images (.jpeg, .bmp, .png, .gif) but with the straight
lines and high contrast of a chart you start running into problems
with visible grainy-ness right away unless you are using extremely
large files. You also don't get the chance to fix individual elements
within the plot using this method, you can only resize and overlay
them.

I realize this is a coding group, and I don't want to take away from
the project. If it can be done in R it would be cool to see how it
gets solved. But, it seems like doing it externally might be alot
quicker unless there is a reason the insets must be done within the
code.

Jens

messages.author: 9ff02ee016b8a9e0
messages.subject: Re: insets of non-ggplot2 plots
parts:
Jens, 

I agree that, without easily implemented methods in R already, combining plots etc. would be faster in external programs. However, I am really trying hard to create reproducible research, including displaying data. Plus, if it can be done in R, it is much faster in the long run to run a line of code after fiddling with code in R, than to make graphs in R, export them, manipulate them in another program, then save that as a jpeg, etc. 

This does basically what I want using base graphics with gridBase:
##############################
require(ape)
require(gridBase)

# make tree
tree <- rtree(20)

# produce outer ("main") plot
quartz()
plot(1:10,xaxs="i",yaxs="i")
vp <- baseViewports()
pushViewport(vp$inner,vp$figure,vp$plot)

# push viewport that will contain the inset
pushViewport(viewport(x=0.1,y=0.9,width=.5,height=.5,just=c("left","top")))

# define viewport to contain the whole inset figure
par(fig=gridFIG(),new=T) # or gridPLT() # ...or just the plotting are (coordinate system)

# draw frame around selected area, not necessary really
grid.rect(gp=gpar(lwd=3,col="red"))

# plot inset figure
plot(tree, no.margin = TRUE)


But, I want to do so with ggplot2 graphics (which I tried and did not work, trying to plot the tree as inset just created a new graphics window). I tried ggExtra a bit, but nothing pops out as what I need. 

Thanks, Scott

You'll need something in base graphics if you want to retrieve the
baseViewports() later, so I suggest,

plot.new() # doesn't draw anything but sets up the page using base graphics
qplot(1:10,1:10) # draw grid graphics on the full device regardless
vp <- baseViewports()

> pushViewport(vp$inner,vp$figure,vp$plot)
> # push viewport that will contain the inset
> pushViewport(viewport(x=0.1,y=0.9,width=.5,height=.5,just=c("left","top")))
> # define viewport to contain the whole inset figure
> par(fig=gridFIG(),new=T) # or gridPLT() # ...or just the plotting are
> (coordinate system)
> # draw frame around selected area, not necessary really
> grid.rect(gp=gpar(lwd=3,col="red"))
> # plot inset figure
> plot(tree, no.margin = TRUE)
>
> But, I want to do so with ggplot2 graphics (which I tried and did not work,
> trying to plot the tree as inset just created a new graphics window). I
> tried ggExtra a bit, but nothing pops out as what I need.
> Thanks, Scott

Indeed, there's nothing like this in ggExtra. It could be a good idea
though, with two functions: i) a ggplot2 inset in a base plot; ii) a
base inset in a ggplot.

HTH,

baptiste
